raw_comment:
Even though Colorado feels pretty dry compared to other states, most of the state doesn't seem to be effected by drought. Only the northern part seems to be suffering from drought.

Why is the area between Ohio and West Virginia suffering from drought if they're next to the Atlantic Ocean and the Great Lakes.

If drought continues south of Colorado, or the Colorado River starts to dry up, states that rely on the river will have to find a different water source and anything that requires water will have to find a different source soon, or it will be quite difficult for lives in those states.

A headline would be "Does your state's land need some moisturizer?"
